sentences.text: This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 15/01/2018 passed by Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar (M.P.) in Claim Case No.217/2015, whereby an amount of Rs.3,06,020/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 12/08/2015 to the appellant / claimant with interest @ 7.5% per annum.

entities.text: Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that income of the injured should have been assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act issued by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, according to which on the date of accident i.e. 19/03/2015 income of the injured comes to Rs.6,175/- considering him 'Skilled Labourer'.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further submits that appellant has suffered grievous injuries.
He has suffered fractures fracture in Tibia Fibula Bone, fracture in Pelvis Bone, crush injuries, non-united fracture and implant has also been installed.
Learned Claims Tribunal has ignored the aforesaid NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8893 2 MA-2506-2018 aspect and awarded meager amount of Rs.3,06,015/- only.

Thus, counsel for the appellant prays for awarding just and proper compensation by giving at least 13% permanent disability by applying multiplier of 17 with 40% future prospects in the light of the judgment delivered by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The amount awarded in other heads i.e. Loss of Income, Attendant Expenses, Conveyance and Special Diet is also on lower side and no amount has been awarded in the head of Loss of Asininities of Life, therefore, at least Rs.25,000/- should have been awarded in this head.

On these grounds,
learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation amount as aforesaid.

1 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
He further submits that the amount awarded in the head of pain and suffering is on higher side, which requires to be reduced to Rs.25,000/-.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance as prayed for.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

From perusal of the award amount, it appears that evidence has not been objectively assessed only lump sum amounts in the heads of Pain and Suffering, Loss of Income, Attendant Expenses,
Conveyance and Special Diet have been awarded.

In the instant case, Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-2)
has given Permanent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8893 3 MA-2506-2018 Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/189) and opined that disability suffered by the appellant is 39%, but looking to the evidence with regard to disability and also looking to the fact that disability certificate has not been issued by Medical Board and Permanent Disability Certificate is not issued in the proportion of whole body, this Court is of the view that at least 13% permanent disability should have been taken.

6. It is not res integra that where the income is not established by any cogent evidence, income is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, according to which considering the injured as 'Skilled Labour' his income comes to Rs.6,175/- per month.
7. Claimant was 26 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , 40% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects and multiplier of 17 is applied.

8. Looking to the injuries and hardship suffered by appellant, this Court is of the view that the amount awarded in the heads of Loss of Income, Attendant Expenses, Conveyance, Special Diet is on lower side, therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.12,350/- (for 2 months), Rs.10,000/-,
Rs.10,000/- and Rs.10,000/-.
Further, in the head of Loss of Amenities of Life an amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded.
The amount awarded in the head of pain and suffering appears on higher side, therefore, the same is reduced to Rs.25,000/- only.

9. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.6,175/- PM + 40% FP X 12 Months Permanent Disability: X Multiplier of 17 =
Rs.17,63,580/-
13% PD comes to Rs.2,29,265/-
 Pain and Suffering: Rs.25,000/-
 Medical Expenses: Rs.2,32,015/-

 Attendant Expenses: Rs.10,000/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8893  4   Conveyance: Rs.10,000/-
 Special Diet: Rs.10,000/-
 Loss of Amenities of Life: Rs.25,000/-
 Total: Rs.5,53,630/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.3,06,015/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.2,47,615/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,53,630/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,06,015/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.2,47,615/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
10. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / claimant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 7.5%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
